title: What Happens To Your Body When You Eat Organic For 6 Days
summary: An herbalist says six days of organic eating sharply cuts body pesticide levels and that washing produce cannot remove residues.

assertions.quote: Just 6 days on organic food dropped the amount of pesticides of all kinds by a huge amount

verdicts.note: All four whole-diet crossover trials (children and adults) that measured urinary pesticide metabolites found significant drops, up to 90%, within a few days of switching to organic.
Systematic review (abstract only): two studies found significantly lower urinary pesticide levels in children eating organic versus conventional diets.

In 16 people from four US families, switching to an organic diet significantly cut urinary levels of 13 pesticide compounds (e.g. malathion metabolite -95%, clothianidin -83%, chlorpyrifos metabolite -61%); abstract only, small uncontrolled pre-post design.

The review reports intervention studies where urinary pesticide excretion fell markedly after one week of eating organic food, and that frequent organic produce eaters have lower urinary pesticide levels.

assertions.quote: 99% of it is inside the produce itself and you can't get rid of it

verdicts.note: PDP rinses every sample 15-20 seconds under cold water as a consumer would, and 57.7% still carried detectable residue, so a rinse leaves residues behind; how much it removed was not measured.

assertions.quote: endocrine endocrine disruptors, you know, all your hormones get thrown off like crazy also

verdicts.note: EWG reports EPA cancelled DCPA in 2024 after data showed even low exposures altered fetal thyroid hormone levels, one example of hormone disruption at low dose, though not shown specifically at dietary levels.

assertions.quote: We have so many cancers now, and this is not a good thing.

verdicts.note: Million Women Study (UK) found no overall cancer reduction except possibly NHL; NutriNet-Sante (France) found 25% lower hazard in top organic quartile (0.6% absolute) mainly for NHL and postmenopausal breast cancer; both observational and confounded.

In 68,946 French adults followed about 4.6 years, the top quartile of organic-food frequency had HR 0.75 for any cancer (absolute risk reduction 0.6%), with signals only for NHL, lymphomas and postmenopausal breast cancer; observational, short follow-up, health-conscious volunteers, residual confounding acknowledged.

In 623,080 UK women followed 9.3 years (53,769 cancers), usually/always eating organic food was not linked to lower total cancer (RR 1.03, 0.99-1.07; 1.00 among consistent consumers), breast cancer was slightly higher (RR 1.09), and only NHL was lower (RR 0.79), which the authors say may be chance.
